rejected_candidates.reason: Section 5.2 step 7 permits task mutation and dispatch after persisted-byte equality and strict PASS without naming the create-once APPLIED `ExecutionTransitionCompletion` that Section 9.1 makes a precondition of dispatchability, so the two dispatch gates differ; rejected as non-material because the charge write itself still requires fresh Section 5.2 step 1-2 P14/P7-P12 PASS, P3 accepts only a complete intent/completion chain and blocks the following charge, an un-finalizable APPLIED preserves the charge in TRANSITION_RECOVERY_BLOCKED, and no reading permits an unready charge, a charge reuse or an acceptance.

Section 6.3 allocates the cumulative AdministrativeResourceLedger ceiling only across bootstrap, migration, post-charge ledger repair, acceptance-projection repair, review recovery and transition-intent finalization/recovery, while ordinary uncharged pre-charge admission work (prepare, bundle seal, boundary observation, capability preflight, reviewer discovery) and the Section 16 uncharged admission proof are assigned to neither that ledger nor the P12 charge ceiling; rejected as non-material because this work is uncharged, consumes no mission attempt and cannot itself permit a charge or an acceptance, and P12 plus the ledger allocations cover the charged attempt, mandatory downstream minima and recovery contingency.

Section 6.1 calls the charge 'one version-guarded `execution.json` update using the runtime's native guarded file write/edit operation' while Section 7 P15 and Section 16 require the P15-bound guarded writer and immutable write-result receipt to be bootstrapped with exact argv/effects; rejected as non-material because the packet's failure-model evidence records the accepted assignment of this class of existing version-guarded native ledger write/edit with explicit no-write abort semantics, Section 5.3 disclaims any non-bypassable native hook, and P15 fails to `NOT_READY` when the guarded writer is absent or unproven, so no unsupported capability can permit a charge.
